doc.title: Jack Palmer interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 24, 1997

title: The early James band and Sinatra's first night as vocalist
summary: The band opened in Philadelphia; James hired Sinatra after seeing him in New Jersey, and Sinatra's first song with the band was Stardust.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: So what kind of schedule did the Harry James band have when they first started out? I mean did you go right into like really on the road type stuff?

We went right to the Benjamin Franklin Hotel in Philadelphia. That was the first appearance. And from there we just did a gang of one nighters, you know, one night stands. And we came back to New York to The Roseland Ballroom and let’s see I started in January, and Frank Sinatra joined us in May. And I remember Harry said, Harry told me about him somewhere along the way, when we were at the Paramount Theatre. He says, “Jack you want to take a ride with me after the last show? I’m going to go see, there’s a kid playing a singing act in New Jersey somewhere” he says, “and I’m going to go catch him.” And, “Do you want to come with me?” And I says, “I can’t, I’ve got people from Rome visiting me and I promised to take them to Chinatown.” So he went, anyway, he took Louise Tobin, his wife. The next morning, after the first show, and just before the second show, evidently Frank had been up in the dressing room, and he came © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-

downstairs before we went into the pit, and Harry introduced him, and they had already signed a contract. Harry says, “Fellas, I want you to meet our new vocalist, Frank Sinatra, and we’ll meet him singly afterwards” you know because we had to go into the pit. And so from that engagement, the next engagement was New Haven, Connecticut and that’s where Frank joined us and Harry introduced him there, and said, “Ladies and gentlemen I’d like to introduce you to our — have you meet our new vocalist, who we don’t have any arrangements for—come on out Frank and say hello to the folks.” And Frank did. Then Harry says “well why don’t you sing something Frank, anyway.” So Frank leaned over to the piano player and says I guess what key he was going to sing. And Harry says, “What are you going to sing, Frank,” and he says, “Stardust.” I never forgot that, that was his first song, without any music, it was just the piano and the rhythm section you know?
That’s a tough song to open up to.
Yeah. But that’s the one he chose and he sang it. I’ll never forget that. Because we thought why did he choose “Stardust” you know, which really was an instrumental more than it was a vocal.
